column1: The Treatise on Architecture: like things grouped, every rule set down.
column2: 《营造法式》：类例相从，条章具在。

column1: Steel stirred and forged a hundred times, hard yet supple.

column2: 铸钱通宝，权衡天下之货。

column1: When the Zhengguo Canal was done, the land within the passes became fertile and knew no famine.
column2: 郑国渠成，关中为沃野，无凶年。

column1: When the granaries are full, the people know propriety.

column2: 分天下以为郡县，郡置守、尉、监。

column1: A craftsman who would do good work must first sharpen his tools.
column2: 工欲善其事，必先利其器。

column1: Orders sent by relay stations travel faster than any rider.

Who excels at learning may serve the state.
A farmer's son at dawn, in the emperor's hall by dusk.
column2: 朝为田舍郎，暮登天子堂。

column1: A million piculs of grain shipped up the canals each year to fill the capital.
column2: 江淮粟帛，岁漕百万石以实京师。

column1: Iron coins weighed too much in Shu, so the people wrote notes and called them jiaozi.
column2: 蜀人以铁钱重，私为券，谓之交子。

column1: Households in tens vouch for each other: soldiers when called, farmers when home.
column2: 什伍相保，出则为兵，入则为农。

column1: The Exploitation of the Works of Nature: prize the five grains above gold and jade.

column2: 因山川形便，分天下为十道。

column1: Branch secretariats set up in every province, to govern the far lands as the near.
column2: 立行中书省，以治远方如近畿。

column1: Estates of the crown in every province, their harvests sent to the capital.
column2: 诸路皆置皇庄，岁输所入于京师。

column1: Commissioners hold the frontier commands, each with his own army and supplies.
column2: 节度使统边镇，兵甲、财赋自专。

column1: Granaries full, the people prosperous, all under heaven at peace.
column2: 仓廪丰实，百姓殷富，天下乂安。

column1: Know the enemy and know yourself: a hundred battles without peril.

column2: 步人甲重五十斤，刀箭不能入。

column1: Galloping and hunting, drawing the bow at full stretch.

column1: Officers chosen by bow and horse, ranked by essays on strategy.
column2: 以弓马取士，以策论定等。
